outcome: No result addressing Ulam's packing conjecture (whether the ball is the worst-packing convex solid) was found published or announced between 26 January 2024 and today; the conjecture remains open with the same partial results (Kallus's local-minimum theorem, and simulation verification for various solid classes) that predate the frozen revision.
summary: I ran a broad set of searches covering the conjecture directly ("Ulam's packing conjecture" with 2024/2025/2026), the underlying mathematical question (worst-packing convex solid, worst packer, asphericity, local minimum), potential counterexamples, and an AI-specific angle. All searches returned only pre-2024 material: Kallus's 2012–2015 local-minimum results for point-symmetric bodies and the ball's local pessimum status in 3D, the Kallus–Nazarov dimension-dependent result (arXiv 1212.2551, from December 2012, showing dimensions 4,5,6,7,8,24 admit small-asphericity bodies that pack worse than balls — this is a pre-window result the triage's 'why' field also surfaced), and simulation-based verification extended to prisms/antiprisms, Johnson solids, and Catalan solids (also pre-2024 work). Two 2024–2026 papers that surfaced in searches — Schildkraut's 'Lower bounds for sphere packing in arbitrary norms' (arXiv 2406.07479, June 2024, revised April 2025) and Han/Henk/Xue's 'Packing minima of convex bodies' (arXiv 2601.13937, January 2026) — were opened directly and neither mentions or relates to Ulam's conjecture: the first is about density lower bounds for sphere packing in general normed spaces (a related but distinct question), and the second is about a different notion of 'packing minima' unconnected to the worst-packer question. A search for AI/ML connections surfaced only a reinforcement-learning paper on kissing numbers (arXiv 2511.13391), which is an unrelated problem (kissing numbers, not Ulam's packing conjecture). The current (2026) Wikipedia article for the conjecture was fetched directly and its full reference list contains no citations after 2015, confirming no update has been logged even informally. I am satisfied nothing has happened to this problem in the window.
competing_reading: None of the tangentially related 2024–2026 papers (sphere packing in arbitrary norms, packing minima, kissing-number RL) constitute even a 'related problem' finding worth recording as `progress`, since none of them mention or bear formally on the specific claim that the ball is the worst-packing convex solid — they address different, only thematically adjacent packing questions. There is no genuine ambiguity here to flag.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or announcement that either proves/disproves Ulam's conjecture in full, exhibits a convex solid packing worse than the ball (a global counterexample), extends the local-minimum result to a broader class of shapes, or explicitly discusses the conjecture by name with a dated 2024+ result.
